NKJV.1: Thus the heavens and the earth, and all the host of them, were finished.
NKJV.2: And on the seventh day God ended His work which He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.
NKJV.3: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because in it He rested from all His work which God had created and made.
NKJV.4: This is the history of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens,
NKJV.5: before any plant of the field was in the earth and before any herb of the field had grown. For the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no man to till the ground;
NKJV.6: but a mist went up from the earth and watered the whole face of the ground.
NKJV.7: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
NKJV.8: The LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden, and there He put the man whom He had formed.
NKJV.9: And out of the ground the LORD God made every tree grow that is pleasant to the sight and good for food. The tree of life was also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
NKJV.10: Now a river went out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it parted and became four riverheads.
NKJV.11: The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one which skirts the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
NKJV.12: And the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and the onyx stone are there.
NKJV.13: The name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one which goes around the whole land of Cush.
NKJV.14: The name of the third river is Hiddekel; it is the one which goes toward the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
NKJV.15: Then the LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to tend and keep it.
NKJV.16: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, “Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat;
NKJV.17: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.”
NKJV.18: And the LORD God said, “It is not good that man should be alone; I will make him a helper comparable to him.”
NKJV.19: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living creature, that was its name.
NKJV.20: So Adam gave names to all cattle, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper comparable to him.
NKJV.21: And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
NKJV.22: Then the rib which the LORD God had taken from man He made into a woman, and He brought her to the man.
NKJV.23: And Adam said: “This is now bone of my bones And flesh of my flesh; She shall be called Woman, Because she was taken out of Man.”
NKJV.24: Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
NKJV.25: And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

NASB.1: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their hosts.
NASB.2: By the seventh day God completed His work which He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.
NASB.3: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because in it He rested from all His work which God had created and made.
NASB.4: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made earth and heaven.
NASB.5: Now no shrub of the field was yet in the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprouted, for the LORD God had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
NASB.6: But a mist used to rise from the earth and water the whole surface of the ground.
NASB.7: Then the LORD God formed man of dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
NASB.8: The LORD God planted a garden toward the east, in Eden; and there He placed the man whom He had formed.
NASB.9: Out of the ground the LORD God caused to grow every tree that is pleasing to the sight and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
NASB.10: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it divided and became four rivers.
NASB.11: The name of the first is Pishon; it flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
NASB.12: The gold of that land is good; the bdellium and the onyx stone are there.
NASB.13: The name of the second river is Gihon; it flows around the whole land of Cush.
NASB.14: The name of the third river is Tigris; it flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
NASB.15: Then the LORD God took the man and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate it and keep it.
NASB.16: The LORD God commanded the man, saying, 'From any tree of the garden you may eat freely;
NASB.17: but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat from it you will surely die.'
NASB.18: Then the LORD God said, 'It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make him a helper suitable for him.'
NASB.19: Out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the sky, and brought [them] to the man to see what he would call them; and whatever the man called a living creature, that was its name.
NASB.20: The man gave names to all the cattle, and to the birds of the sky, and to every beast of the field, but for Adam there was not found a helper suitable for him.
NASB.21: So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept; then He took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh at that place.
NASB.22: The LORD God fashioned into a woman the rib which He had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.
NASB.23: The man said, 'This is now bone of my bones, And flesh of my flesh; She shall be called Woman, Because she was taken out of Man.'
NASB.24: For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother, and be joined to his wife; and they shall become one flesh.
NASB.25: And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed.

NLT.1: So the creation of the heavens and the earth and everything in them was completed.
NLT.2: On the seventh day God had finished his work of creation, so he rested from all his work.
NLT.3: And God blessed the seventh day and declared it holy, because it was the day when he rested from all his work of creation.
NLT.4: This is the account of the creation of the heavens and the earth. The Man and Woman in Eden When the LORD God made the earth and the heavens,
NLT.5: neither wild plants nor grains were growing on the earth. For the LORD God had not yet sent rain to water the earth, and there were no people to cultivate the soil.
NLT.6: Instead, springs came up from the ground and watered all the land.
NLT.7: Then the LORD God formed the man from the dust of the ground. He breathed the breath of life into the man’s nostrils, and the man became a living person.
NLT.8: Then the LORD God planted a garden in Eden in the east, and there he placed the man he had made.
NLT.9: The LORD God made all sorts of trees grow up from the ground — trees that were beautiful and that produced delicious fruit. In the middle of the garden he placed the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
NLT.10: A river flowed from the land of Eden, watering the garden and then dividing into four branches.
NLT.11: The first branch, called the Pishon, flowed around the entire land of Havilah, where gold is found.
NLT.12: The gold of that land is exceptionally pure; aromatic resin and onyx stone are also found there.
NLT.13: The second branch, called the Gihon, flowed around the entire land of Cush.
NLT.14: The third branch, called the Tigris, flowed east of the land of Asshur. The fourth branch is called the Euphrates.
NLT.15: The LORD God placed the man in the Garden of Eden to tend and watch over it.
NLT.16: But the LORD God warned him, “You may freely eat the fruit of every tree in the garden —
NLT.17: except the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. If you eat its fruit, you are sure to die.”
NLT.18: Then the LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper who is just right for him.”
NLT.19: So the LORD God formed from the ground all the wild animals and all the birds of the sky. He brought them to the man to see what he would call them, and the man chose a name for each one.
NLT.20: He gave names to all the livestock, all the birds of the sky, and all the wild animals. But still there was no helper just right for him.
NLT.21: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. While the man slept, the LORD God took out one of the man’s ribs and closed up the opening.
NLT.22: Then the LORD God made a woman from the rib, and he brought her to the man.
NLT.23:
“At last!” the man exclaimed. “This one is bone from my bone,
and flesh from my flesh!
She will be called ‘woman,’
because she was taken from ‘man.’”
NLT.24: This explains why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and the two are united into one.
NLT.25: Now the man and his wife were both naked, but they felt no shame.

CSB17.16: And the LORD God commanded the man, “You are free to eat from any tree of the garden, <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.17: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for on the day you eat from it, you will certainly die.” <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.18: Then the LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper corresponding <sup>ⓜ</sup> to him.”
CSB17.19: The LORD God formed out of the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky, and brought each to the man to see what he would call it. <sup>ⓝ</sup> And whatever the man called a living creature, that was its name.

CSB17.22: Then the LORD God made the rib he had taken from the man into a woman and brought her to the man. <sup>ⓑ</sup>

And the man said: This one, at last, is bone of my bone
and flesh of my flesh;
this one will be called “woman,”
for she was taken from man. ⓒ

WEB.9: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
WEB.10: A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
WEB.11: The name of the first is Pishon: it flows through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
WEB.12: and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium  and onyx stone are also there.
WEB.13: The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the same river that flows through the whole land of Cush.
WEB.14: The name of the third river is Hiddekel. This is the one which flows in front of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
WEB.15: Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
WEB.16: Yahweh God commanded the man, saying, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;
WEB.17: but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
WEB.18: Yahweh God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to  him.”
WEB.19: Out of the ground Yahweh God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.
WEB.20: The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him.
WEB.21: Yahweh God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
WEB.22: Yahweh God made a woman from the rib which he had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.
WEB.23: The man said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She will be called ‘woman,’ because she was taken out of Man.”
WEB.24: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
WEB.25: The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

AMP.1: So the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their hosts (inhabitants).
AMP.2: And by the seventh day God completed His work which He had done, and He rested (ceased) on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.
AMP.3: So God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it [as His own, that is, set it apart as holy from other days], because in it He rested from all His work which He had created and done.
AMP.4: This is the history of [the origin of] the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day [that is, days of creation] that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens—
AMP.5: no shrub or plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprouted, for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground,
AMP.6: but a mist (fog, dew, vapor) used to rise from the land and water the entire surface of the ground—
AMP.7: then the LORD God formed [that is, created the body of] man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and the man became a living being [an individual complete in body and spirit].
AMP.8: And the LORD God planted a garden (oasis) in the east, in Eden (delight, land of happiness); and He put the man whom He had formed (created) there.
AMP.9: And [in that garden] the LORD God caused to grow from the ground every tree that is desirable and pleasing to the sight and good (suitable, pleasant) for food; the tree of life was also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the [experiential] knowledge (recognition) of [the difference between] good and evil.
AMP.10: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it divided and became four [branching] rivers.
AMP.11: The first [river] is named Pishon; it flows around the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.
AMP.12: The gold of that land is good; bdellium (a fragrant, valuable resin) and the onyx stone are found there.
AMP.13: The name of the second river is Gihon; it flows around the entire land of Cush [in Mesopotamia].
AMP.14: The third river is named Hiddekel (Tigris); it flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
AMP.15: So the LORD God took the man [He had made] and settled him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
AMP.16: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, "You may freely (unconditionally) eat [the fruit] from every tree of the garden;
AMP.17: but [only] from the tree of the knowledge (recognition) of good and evil you shall not eat, otherwise on the day that you eat from it, you shall most certainly die [because of your disobedience]."
AMP.18: Now the LORD God said, "It is not good (beneficial) for the man to be alone; I will make him a helper [one who balances him—a counterpart who is] suitable and complementary for him."
AMP.19: So the LORD God formed out of the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them; and whatever the man called a living creature, that was its name.
AMP.20: And the man gave names to all the livestock, and to the birds of the air, and to every animal of the field; but for Adam there was not found a helper [that was] suitable (a companion) for him.
AMP.21: So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam; and while he slept, He took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh at that place.
AMP.22: And the rib which the LORD God had taken from the man He made (fashioned, formed) into a woman, and He brought her and presented her to the man.
AMP.23:
Then Adam said,
"This is now bone of my bones,
And flesh of my flesh;
She shall be called Woman,
Because she was taken out of Man."
AMP.24: For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and they shall become one flesh.
AMP.25: And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed or embarrassed.

NET.1: The heavens and the earth were completed with everything that was in them.
NET.2: By the seventh day God finished the work that he had been doing, and he ceased on the seventh day all the work that he had been doing.
NET.3: God blessed the seventh day and made it holy because on it he ceased all the work that he had been doing in creation.
NET.4: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created — when the LORD God made the earth and heavens.
NET.5: Now no shrub of the field had yet grown on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprouted, for the LORD God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
NET.6: Springs would well up from the earth and water the whole surface of the ground.
NET.7: The LORD God formed the man from the soil of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.
NET.8: The LORD God planted an orchard in the east, in Eden; and there he placed the man he had formed.
NET.9: The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow from the soil, every tree that was pleasing to look at and good for food. (Now the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil were in the middle of the orchard.)
NET.10: Now a river flows from Eden to water the orchard, and from there it divides into four headstreams.
NET.11: The name of the first is Pishon; it runs through the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.
NET.12: (The gold of that land is pure; pearls and lapis lazuli are also there).
NET.13: The name of the second river is Gihon; it runs through the entire land of Cush.
NET.14: The name of the third river is Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
NET.15: The LORD God took the man and placed him in the orchard in Eden to care for it and to maintain it.
NET.16: Then the LORD God commanded the man, “You may freely eat fruit from every tree of the orchard,
NET.17: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it you will surely die.”
NET.18: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a companion for him who corresponds to him.”
NET.19: The LORD God formed out of the ground every living animal of the field and every bird of the air. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them, and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
NET.20: So the man named all the animals, the birds of the air, and the living creatures of the field, but for Adam no companion who corresponded to him was found.
NET.21: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he was asleep, he took part of the man’s side and closed up the place with flesh.
NET.22: Then the LORD God made a woman from the part he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man.
NET.23: Then the man said, “This one at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; this one will be called ‘woman,’ for she was taken out of man.”
NET.24: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and unites with his wife, and they become a new family.
NET.25: The man and his wife were both naked, but they were not ashamed.
